name: Split Word Essay
note: Script splits each block into per-word spans inside overflow-hidden masks, then an IntersectionObserver rooted to the reading pane lifts them from below on a 55ms cascade.
html:
Field notes4 min read

Type arrives one word at a time

Every word sits in its own mask, so a line can rise out of nothing without the paragraph reflowing around it.

Reveals follow reading order

Delays stack left to right at fifty-five milliseconds, roughly the pace of a comfortable skim down the column.

A reveal that outruns the reader is just a delay with better manners.

Nothing moves until it is seen

The observer is rooted to this pane, so a heading parked below the fold costs nothing until you scroll to it.

name: Defogging Glossary
note: Entries enter from blur(11px) with widened letter-spacing and settle to sharp type as an IntersectionObserver rooted to the list toggles them, while a sticky letter index tracks whichever section is crossing the top band.
html:
ADesign glossary9 terms

Blending edge pixels with the background so a curve reads as smooth rather than stepped at 1x density.

A repeating 4px rhythm every text block snaps to, so columns of unrelated copy still line up across a page.

A ramp of one hue at fixed lightness steps, tuned so any two adjacent steps stay distinguishable on dark surfaces.

Instructions inside a font that nudge stems onto the pixel grid at small sizes, keeping stroke weight even.

A variable axis that thickens hairlines and opens counters as the point size falls, instead of scaling one master.

Rounding a transformed layer to whole device pixels once motion ends, so text stops shimmering mid-animation.

Uniform letter-spacing applied across a run of text, tightened at display sizes and opened for small caps.

Line height and margins chosen as multiples of one unit, so the page keeps a steady beat as blocks stack.

A short, named list of stacking levels every surface must map to, replacing ad-hoc z-index numbers.

name: Per-Letter Manifesto
note: Script splits each headline into per-character spans inside overflow-hidden masks, then an IntersectionObserver rooted to the reading pane rolls every letter up from 105% on a 26ms index-driven delay.
html:
Product principles · 2026

01

Make it obvious

If someone has to guess what a control does, the control is unfinished. Label the verb, show the result.

02

Default to reversible

Every destructive path gets an undo before it gets a confirmation dialog. Confidence comes from being able to step back.

03

Latency is design

A screen that answers in 80ms feels different from one that answers in 400ms, no matter how it is drawn.

04

Write it down

A decision that only lives in a meeting gets remade every quarter. Put the reasoning next to the code.
